paths.description: Homepage and primary video-listing template; covers discovery, navigation, responsive layout, privacy, performance and crawlability.
Hindi category archive, representative of taxonomy/listing pages.
Representative video detail and playback-entry page; playback was not started, but the player, metadata and controls were inspected.
Contact and content-removal form, representing the primary form and recovery journey.
Unknown URL used to inspect HTTP/error recovery behavior.

findings.summary: Transport and cookie defenses are incomplete
findings.evidence: HTTPS and nosniff/X-Frame-Options are present, but CSP is missing, HSTS is effectively disabled with max-age=0, and three first-party cookies are not Secure and use SameSite=None.
findings.suggestedFix: Set meaningful HSTS, deploy a nonce/hash-based CSP, and mark all HTTPS cookies Secure with the narrowest workable SameSite.

findings.summary: Tracking and fingerprint-like ad requests run before consent
findings.evidence: Before any consent action, the page contacts three third-party origins including Google Analytics and two ad-tech domains; request URLs include fingerprint-like screen, plugin, language, canvas/WebGL and timing parameters, while the banner offers no reject choice.
findings.suggestedFix: Block analytics/ad vendors until valid consent, minimize collected parameters, audit vendors and prefer privacy-preserving first-party measurement.

findings.summary: Consent design offers acceptance without equivalent refusal
findings.evidence: Analytics/ad-tech collection starts before consent, while the blocking notice states continued use implies consent and provides Accept but no equally available Reject option.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide Reject all beside Accept, do not load optional vendors first, and make later withdrawal easy.

findings.summary: Cookie notice obscures core content on load
findings.evidence: On first load the cookie notice overlays the bottom of every captured template; on 360x800 it obscures a substantial portion of the next video card and offers only Accept plus a policy link.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace the blocking overlay with a compact, non-obscuring consent surface that offers symmetric choices.

findings.summary: Touch targets are too small and hidden links remain tabbable
findings.evidence: The focus/geometry probe found key cookie and search controls only 21px high, far below a comfortable touch target, while several hidden-menu links remain focusable with 0x0 geometry.
findings.suggestedFix: Raise interactive targets toward 44 CSS px and remove collapsed-menu descendants from sequential focus until opened.

findings.summary: 404 state masquerades as a normal listing
findings.evidence: An unknown URL returns a page visually indistinguishable from a random video listing, with no clear "not found" state, explanation, or recovery action.
findings.suggestedFix: Render an explicit 404 heading and status message with search, home and category recovery actions.

findings.summary: Video lacks captions and controls are undersized
findings.evidence: The layout reflows without horizontal overflow, but key controls are only 21px tall and the representative video element exposes zero text tracks/captions.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide accurate caption tracks/equivalents and enlarge touch controls while preserving zoom/reflow.

findings.summary: Titles and descriptions are extreme, repetitive keyword strings
findings.evidence: The homepage title is 750 characters and description 705 characters; category/detail/contact titles are 161-206 characters, making snippets repetitive and non-descriptive despite tags existing.
findings.suggestedFix: Write unique concise titles and human descriptions for each template/entity, rather than appending the full keyword block.

findings.summary: hreflang and sitemap signals are inconsistent
findings.evidence: Key public pages have canonicals and return 200, but root hreflang alternates point to /sitemap.xml-style URLs rather than equivalent localized pages; /sitemap.xml itself returned a styled 404 while robots points elsewhere to sitemap_index.xml.
findings.suggestedFix: Point hreflang to equivalent localized pages, use x-default where appropriate, and expose only the canonical sitemap index in robots.

findings.summary: Browser-enforced defense headers are incomplete
findings.evidence: Clickjacking and referrer defenses exist, but CSP/frame-ancestors is absent, HSTS max-age is zero, Permissions-Policy is absent, and Lighthouse found third-party cookie issues.
findings.suggestedFix: Add Permissions-Policy, meaningful HSTS and CSP frame-ancestors/Trusted Types where appropriate.

findings.summary: Missing routes have no truthful recovery state
findings.evidence: The tested missing URL presents normal random content instead of a distinct not-found state with a retry/home/search recovery message.
findings.suggestedFix: Create explicit HTTP/network failure templates with useful retry, search and return navigation.

findings.summary: Predominantly Hindi pages declare English
findings.evidence: All four representative pages declare html lang="en-US" although the primary headings, labels and descriptions are predominantly Hindi; direction is undeclared and root hreflang wiring targets sitemap URLs.
findings.suggestedFix: Set accurate per-page lang (for example hi), mark mixed-language passages, and repair locale alternates.

findings.summary: Image delivery wastes hundreds of kilobytes
findings.evidence: Although all images use modern formats, 41/42 are oversized and lack responsive srcset; Lighthouse estimates 562KiB avoidable image transfer.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve responsive WebP/AVIF sizes, reserve dimensions and prioritise only the actual LCP image.

findings.summary: Third-party and image budget is disproportionate before interaction
findings.evidence: Eight third-party requests transfer about 67.7KiB before consent and 41 images account for 1.32MB; this is disproportionate for an unplayed catalog view.
findings.suggestedFix: Set explicit third-party/image budgets, defer optional vendors and load media only on demand.

findings.summary: Hard-coded theme ignores the user color-scheme preference
findings.evidence: Computed-style probe reports colorScheme "normal", no theme media rule, and the normal and emulated-dark screenshots are identical; the design is hard-coded dark rather than preference-driven.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and use prefers-color-scheme/light-dark() so browser chrome and surfaces follow the user.

findings.summary: Custom DIV overlays replace platform primitives
findings.evidence: DOM inspection found #cookie-bar as a plain DIV and #wpst-user-modal as a DIV role=dialog rather than dialog/popover primitives with declarative dismissal.
findings.suggestedFix: Implement transient UI with popover and modal flows with dialog, including declarative close/light-dismiss behavior.

findings.summary: Lab LCP narrowly misses the good threshold
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP 2,636ms, just outside the 2.5s good threshold, despite excellent CLS 0.00016 and TBT 13ms; the independent trace was faster (LCP 802ms).
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritise the first visible poster, reduce blocking work and verify LCP below 2.5s under mobile throttling.

findings.summary: Parser-blocking legacy resources delay rendering
findings.evidence: HAR/DOM confirmation shows parser-blocking jQuery and jQuery Migrate in head plus four blocking stylesheets; Lighthouse estimates 180ms render-blocking savings and the HAR records 74 requests/1.73MB.
findings.suggestedFix: Defer non-critical scripts, remove jQuery Migrate where possible, inline only critical CSS and cache static resources well.

findings.summary: Large unused and unminified code ships on the homepage
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found about 39KiB unused in g2.js, 80% of the theme stylesheet unused on this template, plus unminified CSS/JS opportunities.
findings.suggestedFix: Conditionally load ad/theme modules, purge template-unused CSS and minify production assets.

findings.summary: Images are oversized and lack responsive candidates
findings.evidence: Doctype/charset and image dimensions are present, but 41 of 42 images lack srcset and are over 2x rendered width; Lighthouse estimates 562KiB image-delivery savings.
findings.suggestedFix: Generate width-based WebP/AVIF variants with srcset/sizes and keep explicit dimensions/aspect-ratio.

findings.summary: Advertising stack triggers deprecated API warnings
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports three deprecated API warnings and DevTools cookie inspector issues, including deprecated Shared Storage/Protected Audience use from the advertising stack.
findings.suggestedFix: Update or remove vendors that use deprecated Shared Storage/Protected Audience APIs and clear DevTools Issues.

findings.summary: Password-only account forms lack modern credential support
findings.evidence: No permission prompt fired on load, but hidden registration/login forms use password fields with empty autocomplete values and no visible WebAuthn/passkey option.
findings.suggestedFix: Add correct autocomplete tokens and offer passkeys/WebAuthn for registration and sign-in.

findings.summary: Standalone manifest has no offline implementation
findings.evidence: The site declares a standalone web app manifest with start_url and icons, but no active service worker controls any representative page, so the installable intent has no offline fallback.
findings.suggestedFix: Either remove misleading standalone app intent or add a service worker with a safe offline shell/fallback.

findings.summary: Forms omit useful autocomplete tokens
findings.evidence: Contact, registration and login text/email/password fields mostly have empty autocomplete tokens, so browsers and password managers cannot reliably assist name, email, URL or credential entry.
findings.suggestedFix: Add name, email, url, username, current-password/new-password and other appropriate autocomplete values.

findings.summary: Account and consent flows are not modern or readily reversible
findings.evidence: Hidden account dialogs expose password-based registration/login but no passkey path, no credential autocomplete tokens, and ad/consent collection is not reversible from the initial banner.
findings.suggestedFix: Offer passkeys, credential autofill and an always-findable privacy/consent control with easy withdrawal.

findings.summary: Below-fold images and ad scripts load eagerly
findings.evidence: The page loads advertising/fingerprinting scripts and 38 below-fold images without native lazy loading; HAR records 74 requests and 1.73MB before user interaction.
findings.suggestedFix: Lazy-load below-fold imagery, defer optional work and stop background vendor traffic until needed/consented.

findings.summary: Navigation swaps are abrupt
findings.evidence: DOM/CSS probe found no ::view-transition rules; navigation between the MPA listing, category, detail and contact templates is an abrupt full-page swap.
findings.suggestedFix: Add progressive cross-document View Transitions for same-origin template navigation and preserve a no-motion fallback.

findings.summary: Long listings provide no scroll-state guidance
findings.evidence: The homepage is 16,740 CSS pixels tall on mobile, but the header/chrome is static and the CSS probe found no scroll timeline or state-aware progress/affordance.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a lightweight scroll progress/position affordance using declarative scroll-state or scroll-driven CSS.

findings.summary: Legacy overlays are manually positioned
findings.evidence: The site ships custom dropdown/modal UI, but the CSS probe found no anchor-name, position-anchor, or position-try rules; overlays are manually themed legacy components.
findings.suggestedFix: Use popover/dialog plus CSS anchor positioning and position-try fallbacks for menus that must stay attached.

findings.summary: Navigation does not guide attention after state changes
findings.evidence: Representative route changes use abrupt document swaps and the long listing offers no progress marker or post-navigation highlight beyond basic current-menu color.
findings.suggestedFix: Preserve focus and add directional transition/highlight cues for route and in-page navigation.

findings.summary: Reusable cards do not respond to their containers
findings.evidence: The CSS probe found zero container rules; reused cards and sidebars adapt only through global viewport CSS rather than their available container.
findings.suggestedFix: Give reusable card/sidebar regions container-type and use @container rules where composition changes.
